findings.text: The operation named wake_up_new_task provides activation of freshly forked tasks. It moves the task to running state, defers processor choice until late to tolerate affinity change and hotplug, refreshes runqueue timing, seeds utilization history, enqueues with initial identity and tracing, evaluates preemption, and invokes an optional class specific woken hook without runqueue pinning.

Fork completion for the extensible scheduler is provided in active and empty build forms that share the name scx_post_fork. The active form marks the child ready, enables it promptly when already assigned to the extensible class, links it into a global collection with optional identifier hashing, and releases fork protection. The alternate form is empty and imposes no action.

Enabling of tasks in the extensible scheduler is exposed through an outer operation named scx_enable_task that delegates to internal setup and then records enabled state. Internal setup validates absence of custody, derives execution weight with special handling for idle policy and adjustment for control groups, invokes optional callbacks for enable and affinity and weight, and orders affinity before weight dependent derivation.

Preemption observation is managed through a global key with reference counting and per task list membership. Increment and decrement operations adjust global enablement, registration attaches a notifier to the current task with a warning when globally disabled, and unregistration detaches without further checks.

Management of compact CPU affinity masks for the extensible scheduler is exposed through initialization and conversion operations. Initialization records base and length and word count and scheduler linkage and source linkage and shard bounds derived from a global table. Conversion populates mask words from a kernel CPU mask, skipping empty ranges and masking partial edge words according to per identifier CPU mapping.

The operation named post_init_entity_util_avg seeds load history for new tasks and distinguishes fair and non fair classes. Non fair tasks receive only a timestamp refresh so that a later switch to fair finds expected state. Fair tasks derive initial utilization from scaled spare capacity, with proportional sharing capped, and runnable history mirrors utilization.

Delivery of preemption notifications to task local observers is provided in active and empty build forms. The active form checks a global key and, when enabled, walks the per task list to invoke sched in callbacks with processor identity or sched out callbacks with the incoming task. The empty form defines the same names as operations that impose no action.

The object named balance_push_callback is exported for load balancing with empty linkage and a handler binding to the push routine. It serves as a reusable completion hook that runqueue code can chain without further initialization in the routed fragment.

Processor switching is entered through a preparation contract before the architectural handover and a completion contract after. Preparation claims the incoming task as on processor and notifies tracing and performance and preemption observers and mapping management while holding the runqueue. Completion releases the outgoing task, handles prior address space teardown with ordering for user return, invalidates stale block timing, notifies incoming observers, and reclaims stack and reference when the predecessor has terminated.

Allocation of memory context identifiers is entered through the operation named mm_get_cid that initially attempts within a configured limit and, on failure, relaxes the processor and retries within the full possible set until success. The underlying attempt scans for a clear bit and claims it atomically, reporting unset on exhaustion or race.
The fork hook named sched_mm_cid_fork is defined in the routed configuration as an empty entry that accepts a task and performs no observable state change.

Enrolment of a task as a user of a memory identifier domain activates the task side flag, links the task into the domain user collection, increments the user count, and refreshes limits and mode, reporting whether a mode transition is required.

Identifier values below the marker named MM_CID_TRANSIT denote plain task resident assignments with none of the markers named MM_CID_ONCPU and MM_CID_TRANSIT and MM_CID_UNSET set. Values at or above that marker denote special states rather than usable assignments.

Clearing of a task side identifier always writes the marker named MM_CID_UNSET but releases the prior allocation back to the domain only when that prior value was task resident. Non resident prior values are discarded without release.

Domain mode management clears a deferred update flag, refreshes limits, derives a per CPU threshold from user count relative to capacity when in per task mode, clears that threshold when user count falls below it in per CPU mode, and flips mode by toggling the bits named MM_CID_TRANSIT and MM_CID_ONCPU only when the threshold presence disagrees with the current per CPU state, with a barrier separating the store from subsequent fixups.

Global identifier fixup after a mode change skips the current task on the assumption that it has already transferred, places running tasks into transit for their current processor, drops identifiers from tasks that are not running, and completes the transition by marking the domain with the marker named MM_CID_ONCPU.

Translation of scheduler weight to control group weight scales by the value named CGROUP_WEIGHT_DFL relative to a fixed base with rounding to nearest and clamps the result within the bounds named CGROUP_WEIGHT_MIN and CGROUP_WEIGHT_MAX.
Translation of a kernel address to an arena offset for the extensible scheduler subtracts the scheduler arena base from the supplied address to yield an unsigned offset.

The macro named SCX_CMASK_NR_WORDS sizes compact affinity masks to reserve a word per block of identifiers plus an additional terminator word, ensuring coverage of the whole requested range even when the length is not a multiple of the block width.

Dispatch of identifier aware scheduler operations for the extensible scheduler forwards to a generic task operation dispatcher bound to the identifier aware operation table, preserving scheduler handle and operation name and locked runqueue and task and extra arguments.

Run delay accounting excludes idle tasks from arrival and departure updates. Arrival clears the queued timestamp, accumulates delay into task and runqueue totals, increments counts, and maintains minimum and maximum extremes with a timestamp for the maximum. Departure accumulates processor time and requeues the timestamp when the task remains runnable. Alternate build forms define the same names as empty operations.

Preparation of scratch affinity storage for scheduler callbacks reuses per processor memory bound to the scheduler, initializes a reference over the full possible range, and mirrors the supplied kernel CPU mask into compact form before handing the storage to the callback.

Propagation of affinity changes to the extensible scheduler branches on identifier aware mode. In that mode it converts the kernel CPU mask to compact scratch form and invokes the compact mask operation. Otherwise it forwards the kernel CPU mask directly to the CPU mask operation.

Correctness of memory identifier management requires holding the domain mutex during global fixup and holding the domain spin lock during user enrolment and limit refresh. The routed fragments assert these holdings and treat violation as a programming error.

Remote access to per processor identifier storage of a memory domain requires holding the runqueue lock of the target task through a scoped guard. Local classification of the task side value may precede the guard, but transit handling and dropping occur under protection.

Enabling of tasks in the extensible scheduler requires holding the associated runqueue, with the fork path acquiring the task runqueue around enablement. Global task linkage and optional identifier hashing occur under a dedicated tasks lock with interrupt discipline, and fork protection is released as a read guard after linkage.

Activation of new tasks holds the task pi lock while marking running state and choosing placement, then holds the selected runqueue while refreshing timing and enqueuing. The runqueue pin is temporarily dropped around the optional class woken hook and reacquired before release.

Runqueue locking across a processor switch follows a handover discipline where the outgoing runqueue is unpinned and released by the incoming task with dependency tracking adjusted. Completion reacquires dependency tracking, drains balance callbacks, exits high resolution tick scheduling, and unlocks with interrupts restored.

The memory side identifier domain observed in the fragments carries the members named mutex and lock and user_list and users and max_cids and mode and pcpu_thrs and update_deferred and pcpu. These members coordinate allocation limits and mode transitions and fixup.

The record named mm_cid observed on tasks carries the members named cid and active and node. The assignment distinguishes usable values from special markers, the flag marks enrolment, and the node chains the task into the domain collection.

Compact affinity storage named scx_cmask carries the members named base and nr_cids and alloc_words and bits. Its reference named scx_cmask_ref carries the members named sch and src and base and nr_cids and shard_first and shard_end. An enable argument bundle carries the member named cmask_arena_addr.

Task delay history named sched_info carries the members named last_queued and last_arrival and run_delay and pcount and min_run_delay and max_run_delay and max_run_delay_ts. Runqueue aggregates carry accumulated delay and a count and processor time under the names run_delay and pcount and rq_cpu_time. A runqueue also exposes the members named idle and curr and prev_mm.

A balance callback carries the members named next and func. A preemption notifier carries the member named link and a table named ops with the hooks named sched_in and sched_out. Task extensible state carries the members named weight and flags and tasks_node and tid_hash_node. Tasks also expose the members named sched_class and cpus_ptr and static_prio and on_cpu and pi_lock and preempt_notifiers and __state.

Memory identifier domains move between per task and per CPU provision with a transit bridge. Per task mode raises a threshold when users exceed capacity. Per CPU mode clears that threshold when users fall below it. Disagreement between threshold presence and current mode triggers a flip that toggles transit and on CPU bits, followed by fixup and completion.

Task side identifiers move among assigned and transit and unset with a domain wide on CPU completion. Assigned values reside below the transit marker. Running tasks under fixup enter transit for their processor. Non running tasks move to unset. Completion marks the domain on CPU to close the transition.

Extensible scheduler tasks move from the state named SCX_TASK_READY to the state named SCX_TASK_ENABLED. Fork completion records ready. Enablement is immediate when the task already belongs to the extensible class and otherwise deferred until a later switch. Successful setup records enabled. Absence of the flag named SCX_TASK_IN_CUSTODY is required at setup and violation is reported.

Processor presence tracked by the member named on_cpu moves through claim before handover and release after. Preparation marks the incoming task present. Completion samples predecessor state, switches timing and performance context, clears presence with release ordering, and, when the predecessor carries the state named TASK_DEAD, invokes class and subsystem hooks before dropping stack and reference.

Queued timestamp state tracked by the member named last_queued moves between set and cleared. Enqueue sets the stamp. Arrival consumes it to compute delay and clears it to prevent reuse. Departure sets it again when the task remains runnable. Absence of a stamp causes arrival to return without update.

Identifier allocation faces exhaustion and race hazards where the underlying attempt reports the marker named MM_CID_UNSET. The outer acquisition mitigates by relaxing the processor and retrying within the full possible set until a usable value appears, which implies unbounded spinning under sustained contention or shortage.

Mode flipping faces a reordering hazard where processor reordering could move runqueue acquisition before the mode store, allowing observers to see fixups without the new mode. The fragments mitigate by separating the store from fixups with a barrier.

Completion of a switch faces a race where a concurrent wakeup could place the predecessor on another processor after presence is cleared but before state is observed, risking a repeated transition from running to dead. The fragments mitigate by sampling predecessor state before clearing presence.

Extensible scheduler setup faces inconsistency hazards where a task arrives with custody already set or identifier hash insertion fails. The fragments report these conditions through warning primitives without altering control flow in the routed code.

Preemption notification faces silent disablement hazards where registration occurs while globally disabled or where empty build forms discard callbacks. The active registration path reports disabled use through a warning primitive but still links the notifier. Empty forms impose no action and provide no diagnostic.

Switch completion faces a corruption hazard where the incoming preemption depth differs from the expected fork baseline, indicating unbalanced disablement or locking. The fragments report the condition in a limited manner and reset the depth to the fork baseline to allow continued execution.

The memory identifier domain distinguishes the markers named MM_CID_TRANSIT and MM_CID_ONCPU and MM_CID_UNSET. Transit marks the boundary for task resident values and participates in mode flips. On CPU marks completion of fixup. Unset marks absence of assignment and allocation failure.

The extensible scheduler distinguishes the task states named SCX_TASK_READY and SCX_TASK_ENABLED and the custody flag named SCX_TASK_IN_CUSTODY. Weight derivation distinguishes the idle weight named WEIGHT_IDLEPRIO and a priority table named sched_prio_to_weight indexed relative to the real time ceiling named MAX_RT_PRIO, with control group bounds named CGROUP_WEIGHT_DFL and CGROUP_WEIGHT_MIN and CGROUP_WEIGHT_MAX.

Task activation and switching distinguish the running state named TASK_RUNNING and the dead state named TASK_DEAD and the fork wake flag named WF_FORK and the enqueue modifiers named ENQUEUE_NOCLOCK and ENQUEUE_INITIAL. These markers define initial placement identity and lifecycle termination.
